user.description: Choose the shower valve to set up.

data_description.address: Mira valves in Bluetooth range that are not set up yet.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Pair with {name}
bluetooth_confirm.description:
{moved}The valve only talks to devices it is paired with, and only accepts a new pairing while it is in pairing mode.

1. Close the Mira app on phones nearby (some valves accept only one connection at a time).
2. Put the valve in pairing mode. On a controller with a button, press and hold it for five seconds until it flashes; on a dial controller use Menu > Settings > Connect. Your manual has the steps for your model. Switching the valve's power off and on also leaves it pairable for a short while.
3. Select **Submit** within about 30 seconds.

If the adapter or proxy below is already paired with the valve, select **Submit** straight away.

The pairing is stored on the adapter or proxy that makes it, so use the one that will stay nearest the valve, and keep only that one able to connect there.

In range and able to connect: {connectable}

pair_failed.title: Pairing with {name} failed
pair_failed.description: Put the valve in pairing mode again, then select **Submit** to retry.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair with {name} again

progress.pair: Connecting to {name}, pairing and reading its outlets and presets. This can take a couple of minutes on a slow link.

error.no_connectable_adapter: No Bluetooth adapter or proxy that can make connections is hearing the valve. An ESPHome proxy needs `active: true`.
error.not_in_pairing_mode: The valve refused to pair (through {source}). It was probably not in pairing mode, or the pairing window had closed.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the valve through {source}: {reason}. Check that the Mira app is closed and the valve is powered.
error.no_longer_in_range: The valve is not being heard by any Bluetooth adapter or proxy. Check that it is powered.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. The Home Assistant log has the details.
error.not_encrypted: The link to the valve came up but could not be encrypted (through {source}). The proxy may need a restart, or it holds no pairing with the valve: put the valve in pairing mode and try again.

abort.already_configured: This valve is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: Setup of this valve is already in progress.
abort.no_devices_found: No Mira valve that is not yet set up was found in Bluetooth range.
abort.not_supported: This device is not a supported Mira valve.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The valve is paired and its outlets and presets were re-read.
abort.wrong_device: The valve that answered is not the one this entry was set up for.
abort.moved: The valve was already set up; its entry now points at its new Bluetooth address and pairing.

not_responding.title: {name} has not answered for an hour
not_responding.description:
Home Assistant can hear {name} but has not been able to read it for at least an hour. Pairing it again is rarely the fix. In this order:

1. Close the Mira app on phones nearby (some valves accept only one connection at a time).
2. Restart the Bluetooth proxy nearest the valve. A proxy can keep accepting connections while its pairing store is stuck.
3. Check that only one proxy able to connect is in range of the valve; the pairing lives on the one that made it.
4. Only if none of that helps, use **Reconfigure** on the integration, with the valve in pairing mode.

This notice clears itself when the valve answers again.

proxy_forgets_bond.title: The Bluetooth proxy near {name} is losing its pairing
proxy_forgets_bond.description:
{name} was paired successfully less than an hour ago and is now refusing the pairing. That is the signature of a Bluetooth proxy that forgets pairings after one connection: ESPHome 2026.10 builds on ESP-IDF 5.5.6, which has this fault (esphome/esphome#21880).

Pairing again will not help: it works once and fails again. Either pin the proxy's framework to ESP-IDF 5.5.5 (`esp32: framework: type: esp-idf, version: 5.5.5`), update it to a release that carries the fix, or use a different adapter. Restarting the proxy gives one more working connection.

This notice clears itself when the valve answers again.

start.name: Start outlet
start.description: Opens this outlet at a temperature and flow given for this start only. Other outlets are left as they are. The values are checked against the outlet's own limits and are not remembered.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Target temperature in °C. Defaults to the Target temperature entity.

flow.name: Flow
flow.description: Flow in litres per minute. Defaults to the Target flow entity.

run_preset.name: Run preset
run_preset.description: Starts the preset of this button and carries it past its warm-up, so that it runs for its own duration with nobody at the shower. On a valve that warms a preset up and then waits (a Mira Platinum), pressing the button only warms up; this action also starts the preset once the water is warm. Water then runs until the preset's timer ends or the valve is stopped.
